co_blob_rock_area.blurb: Blob Rock Area is in Boulder Canyon at about 7,100 feet, on the canyon's sunny north side, which makes it a good fit for cooler weather. It mixes multi-pitch trad, older runout face climbs and newer bolted sport routes. Trad makes up about two thirds of the climbs, grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, and the bulk fall between 5.10 and 5.12. A trail climbs from the road to the main wall in roughly 10 to 15 minutes. Blob Rock itself is a large south-facing formation with routes from one-pitch sport to four-pitch trad, East Blob adds old face climbs and well-bolted sport lines, and Small Package Block and Little Blob are small rocks nearby.

ct_ragged_mountain.blurb: Ragged Mountain is a ridge of traprock, a basalt, in the towns of Southington and Berlin, a few miles west of New Britain, Connecticut. It forms part of the Metacomet Ridge, and its cliffs are vertical faces. Climbing is centered on the Main Cliff, which holds essentially all of the climbs here. The routes are mostly trad, with a good number of top-rope lines and a single boulder problem. Grades range from 5.3 up to 5.12, with the greatest numbers between 5.8 and 5.11, so there is a decent supply of easier climbs as well as harder ones.

nm_mentmore.blurb: Mentmore is a sandstone crag in Gallup, New Mexico, with single-pitch routes on well-cemented, yellow to tan Cretaceous sandstone. It is split into two sides, a New Side that holds more of the climbs and an Original Side. Sport routes make up the majority, with a fair number of trad lines and some top-rope climbs, and grades run from the 5.5s to 5.13. The largest groups sit at 5.10 and 5.11, though there is a good supply of easier routes too. Climbing is possible year-round, and winter days can be warm in the sun, while July and August bring the rainy season.

qc_mount_orford_pic_aux_corbeaux.blurb: Pic aux Corbeaux is the main cliff in Parc du Mont Orford, in Quebec's Cantons-de-l'Est off Highway 10 between Sherbrooke and Montreal. The rock is gneiss, solid but rather sharp on crimps, and wet in places. It is mainly a sport-climbing wall, with most routes between 5.9 and 5.13, a few easier ones, and a little trad and mixed. The climbs suit intermediate and expert climbers, and a steep hike of about half an hour leads up to the base. Orford Bouldering adds a set of boulder problems, some along the way up. Les surplombs, Le petit mur and Le grand mur hold the most climbs.

va_labyrinth.blurb: The Labyrinth is a bouldering area in the High Knob Landform of Southwest Virginia, near the reservoir and a short drive above Flag Rock. It is a tightly packed field of freestanding sandstone boulders, many of them tall, with plenty of lower blocks as well. Most of the tall boulders have flat landings. Nearly everything here is a boulder problem, from V0 to V7, with the largest numbers between V1 and V4 and a smaller group of harder lines. Its many separate boulders include Origins Boulder, White Dwarf Boulder and Devil's Boulder.

wi_grandad_bluff.blurb: Grandad Bluff rises above La Crosse, Wisconsin, with views over the Mississippi River. The climbing is mostly sport, on routes bolted with glue-in bolts and fitted with lowering anchors, with a set of boulder problems and a few top-rope lines. Sport grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, with most between 5.9 and 5.11, and boulder problems are mostly V0 to V3. The routes are spread across several separate walls reached on short walks from the parking area. The Miner's Boulders hold the most climbs, followed by George's Point, Adidas Wall and Meader Wall.
